full_judgment: 20. Now during the hearing, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties candidly submits that factually the opposite parties possess only 07 decimals of land.But, it appears from the deposition of DW 1 that they are no more Purohit of the Deity rather, they are engaged in the photo framing business. Thus, they cannot claim any portion of the debutter property in the capacity of purohit. The Sebait also cannot transfer any debutter property. On these points, in the case of Bangladesh vs Abdul Hye and others, 24 BLT (AD) 340 the Appellate Division held that a 'Poojari' is a servant of the Sebait, and no part of the rights and obligations of the latter are transferrable to him. When the appointment of a 'Purohit' has been at the will of the founder, the mere fact that the appointee has performed the worship for several generations will not confer an independent right upon the members of the family so appointed and will not entitle them as of right to be continued in office as priests. Thus, the suit property was not transferrable by the Sebait in favour of Puma Chandra predecessor of the defendants nor can they claim any title in the suit property as of right as the sons of the then 'Purohit'. Both the Courts below failed to consider that the Debutter property cannot be claimed as personal property by any person whatever might be his status. Accordingly, both the Courts below also failed to appreciate that the subsequent SA and BRS records prepared in the names of the opposite parties, or their predecessor have no legal basis inasmuch as the entire property being debutter property without any reservation, the same is beyond the scope and application of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as per section 20(5)(ii)(c) thereof and accordingly, nobody can claim any tenancy right in the debutter property under the Government.
